title: Walsh character under a bit flip
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq[n]$, let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and let $i\in[n]$. The Walsh character satisfies $\chi_S(x^i)=-\chi_S(x)$ if $i\in S$, and $\chi_S(x^i)=\chi_S(x)$ if $i\notin S$.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is in the Boolean hypercube of dimension $n$
